title: Prospective intraoperative in-vivo hyperspectral imaging for assessment of spinal cord perfusion in acute and chronic spinal cord pathologies
summary:
Spinal cord diseases can cause severe neurological impairment. During surgery, it is currently not possible to directly assess spinal cord blood flow.
This study uses a special camera during surgery to measure spinal cord perfusion and oxygenation without contact or contrast agents. These measurements are compared with patients’ clinical status to improve surgical safety and outcomes in the future.
conditions: Acute and chronic spinal cord disorders requiring surgical decompression.

interventions.name:
Single-arm, monocentric, prospective observational study.
Adult patients undergoing surgical spinal cord decompression receive intraoperative, contact-free, contrast-agent-free hyperspectral imaging of the spinal cord. Imaging is performed at standardized time points during surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients (≥ 18 years)

Indication for surgical spinal cord decompression

Acute or chronic spinal cord pathology of traumatic, degenerative, inflammatory, or neoplastic origin

Ability to provide informed consent

Written informed consent for study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Minors

Pregnancy or breastfeeding

Inability to provide informed consent

Refusal to participate in the study

Emergency surgery without possibility of prior informed consent
